Index.heroTitle: At our clinic, we provide testing and diagnosis for dental metal allergies.
Index.heroDescription: If you are experiencing recurring skin symptoms and suspect that metals in the oral cavity may be a contributing factor, please feel free to consult with us.

Symptoms.introTitle: Are you experiencing any of these symptoms?
Symptoms.text1: Metal allergy is an allergic reaction that occurs when the body comes into contact with certain metals and may cause symptoms such as itching of the skin (as shown in the image).
Symptoms.text2: In recent years, the number of individuals with metal allergies has increased, and reactions to metals used in dental treatment are also becoming more common.
Symptoms.text3: At Tokushima University Hospital, we offer a specialized clinic for patients with metal allergies related to dental materials.
Symptoms.guideDocument: Pamphlet: Enjoying Accessories Safely (PDF, Japanese only)

Patch.introTitle: Testing for metal allergies is performed using a patch test, rather than a blood test.
Patch.text1: During the test, special adhesive patches containing small amounts of various metals are applied to the back and left in place for two days.
Patch.text2: After the patches are removed, the skin reaction is evaluated over three follow-up visits. This helps determine whether you have an allergy to specific metals.
Patch.text3: If the test confirms an allergy to a particular metal, and that metal is used in dental treatment in your oral cavity, removal of the material may be recommended depending on your condition. In such cases, we will provide information to your regular dentist and work in coordination to ensure appropriate treatment.
Patch.moreInfo: Download the Metal Allergy Clinic guide here (PDF, Japanese only)
Patch.observation1: * All four visits are required to complete the patch test.
Patch.observation2: * Patch testing is not available in July and August due to increased sweating.

Articles.menu2: Would you like to know what metals are present?
Articles.content1P1:
Metal allergy occurs when metals that come into contact with the skin or oral mucosa dissolve into ions and bind with proteins in the body, forming new substances. These substances may be recognized by the body as foreign, triggering an allergic reaction. 
Metal allergies are broadly classified into contact dermatitis and systemic metal allergy.
Articles.content1P2: Contact dermatitis, commonly referred to as a skin rash, occurs when the skin reacts to substances it comes into contact with, such as metal accessories (e.g., necklaces and earrings), rubber products, cosmetics, medications, or plants. Symptoms may include redness, itching, rashes, or blisters.
Articles.content1P3:
Metals such as nickel are also found in foods including chocolate, cocoa, legumes, spices, shellfish, and whole grains. In addition, many dental materials contain metals such as palladium, gold, and tin. These metals can be absorbed through the skin, mucosa, gastrointestinal tract, and respiratory tract. 
In patients with metal allergy, absorption of these metals may lead to dermatitis affecting the hands, feet, oral cavity, or the entire body. This condition is known as systemic metal dermatitis (systemic metal allergy).
Articles.content2Title: Would you like to know what metals are present?
Articles.content2P1: At our clinic, we also offer elemental analysis of metal samples.
Articles.content2P2: Using an X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzer, we can identify the types of metals contained in dental restorations—such as fillings, crowns, and dentures—as well as in metal products like earrings and necklaces, without damaging them.
Articles.content2P3: By comparing these results with the findings of the patch test, we can help determine which dental materials may need to be removed and which metal products should be avoided.
Articles.content2P4: Metal analysis is available at our clinic as a non-insured service (self-pay). If you would like to request an analysis, please contact the clinic.
Articles.content3P1: In recent years, an increasing number of people have experienced skin problems such as redness, swelling, and irritation after wearing earrings.
Articles.content3P2: If earrings are worn before the piercing site has fully healed, metals may dissolve and enter the body, potentially leading to metal allergy.
Articles.content3P3: To help prevent metal allergy, we recommend using earrings properly and safely by following the points below:
Articles.content3P4: Do not pierce your ears yourself. Have your ears pierced at a medical institution such as a dermatology clinic, cosmetic clinic, or plastic surgery clinic.
Articles.content3P5: Follow the instructions provided and keep the area clean and properly disinfected until it has fully healed.
Articles.content3P6: If the skin is injured when inserting earrings, remove them and wait until the area has healed.
Articles.content3P7: Very inexpensive earrings may release metal due to sweating. It is important to choose products made from materials that are less likely to release metal.
Articles.content3P8: If you experience symptoms such as itching, redness, swelling, or discharge while wearing earrings, discontinue use immediately and consult a dermatologist or other medical professional.

Research.researchTitle: ASMI: Association for Safe Use of Metal Items
Research.text1: We welcome individuals and organizations who are interested in our activities related to metal allergy and the safety of metal products.
Research.text2: Working in collaboration with healthcare professionals, researchers, industry, and public institutions, we aim to promote a safer environment in which consumers can confidently select and use metal products.
Research.text3: If you are interested in contributing to these efforts, we encourage you to consider joining us.
Research.joinButton: Learn more about our Research Group.

Footer.copyright: Research Group on Metal Allergy and Product Safety

ResearchPage.heroTitle: ASMI: Association for Safe Use of Metal Items
ResearchPage.introText1: A wide variety of metal accessories and everyday products are an essential part of our daily lives.
ResearchPage.introText2: However, numerous cases have been reported in which metallic components contained in these products cause skin irritation or allergic reactions through contact with the skin, sometimes resulting in adverse health effects. It is estimated that a significant number of people in Japan, particularly women, are affected by metal allergies.
ResearchPage.introText3: Metal allergy is a condition that can often be prevented through the appropriate use of products that do not release metal ions.
ResearchPage.introText4: To ensure that consumers can safely choose and use metal products, legal measures are needed, including regulations on metal release levels and product labeling requirements.
ResearchPage.introText5: In collaboration with industry and governmental organizations, we are working to create an environment in which consumers can confidently select and use metal products.
ResearchPage.introText6: The statement of purpose is available here. (PDF, Japanese only )
ResearchPage.activitiesText1: We engage in the following activities:
ResearchPage.activitiesText2: Advocacy for the establishment and strengthening of safety standards for metal products
ResearchPage.activitiesText3: Providing information and raising awareness regarding the safety of metal products
ResearchPage.activitiesText4: Research on safety testing and certification systems for metal products
ResearchPage.activitiesText5: Collection of consumer feedback and complaints, and development of improvement proposals based on these insights
ResearchPage.activitiesText6: Organization of lectures and seminars to promote the use of safe metal products
ResearchPage.activitiesText7: The association’s regulations are available here. (PDF, Japanese only )
ResearchPage.membersText: Our activities are carried out through collaboration among physicians, dentists, researchers, and consumer affairs advisors, integrating medical and dental expertise with practical experience in consumer consultation.
ResearchPage.joinText1: We welcome individuals and organizations who are interested in supporting our activities.

home.greetingText: The Department of Stomatognathic Function and Occlusal Reconstruction belongs to the field of prosthodontics — the restoration of teeth that have been badly damaged or lost, using crowns, dentures and similar appliances. Losing teeth makes food harder to eat and speech harder to form, and it disrupts everyday life. It hardly needs saying that eating is fundamental to human life, and that eating well matters a great deal. With that in mind, our department pursues research into how lost teeth can be restored, how the jaw moves, how grinding occurs during the night, what metal allergy involves, and how temporomandibular disorders and orofacial pain should be diagnosed and treated — always working to translate that research into treatment. We hope this work, in the laboratory and in the clinic alike, will help people chew well and so contribute to human wellbeing. We also aim to provide the most current treatment available, working together with other departments and specialist clinics at Tokushima University Hospital. Our staff are committed as one to patient-centred care founded on informed consent, and to prosthodontic treatment of the highest quality.
